One commenter felt Auth0 is "one of those products that shouldn't exist," arguing you're paying a lot for what you can do yourself with a JWT.

A paying Auth0 customer who uses it only for authentication said it saved them about a hundred hours of work for a pretty reasonable price. They argued Auth0 is better at building scalable, secure, resilient auth than most dev teams.
Another user said Auth0 is not reasonably priced for their use case because they need neither its scalability nor all its features. They find Gotrue or SuperTokens fine instead.
During the April 2021 Auth0 outage, a user had an SSO demo for their organization that wasn't working. They panicked over what went wrong and had to skip the demo.
A podcast co-host who covers outages noted that Auth0's 2018 outage was caused by several factors, starting with silently losing some database indexes during a migration.
An Auth0 user said their team was already considering moving to Okta. In their view, Auth0's offering "has always been slightly rough around the edges" and led to slightly suboptimal implementations.
One developer called Cognito a nightmare with many broken things. They lost 3 weeks in February trying to get it working on a project, then integrated Auth0 in 2 days.
A commenter called Cognito and Firebase "bush league" by comparison: they handle the basics if you have the right integration engineers, while Okta and Auth0 are "light years ahead."

One user likes that Auth0's Universal Login page didn't require JavaScript. They fear the Okta acquisition will bring forced migration off .auth0.com domains, a move to Okta's login implementation, and changed client IDs, secrets and M2M setups.

A commenter said Auth0 has been "on the ball" with its open source packages, while Okta's get little attention and often need forks. They found Auth0's interfaces pleasant from both a user and developer perspective, unlike Okta's disjointed, confusing ones.
"Their product solves a really tricky, undifferentiated problem that I'm glad I don't have to solve anymore."
"stormpath > auth0 > okta > ?? ... This will be the third time I've updated my deployments." The user complained about repeated migrations caused by acquisitions.

A user asked how to migrate users away from Auth0 as seamlessly as possible when using its Database connection. They recalled having to raise a support ticket to get an export that includes password hashes.

One developer said they really liked Auth0 and planned to adopt it soon. After the Okta acquisition, they now see a huge risk of a migration nightmare and unknown pricing changes for a critical piece of their app, so they won't adopt it.
A team that came from Auth0 (and "god-awful" Amazon Cognito) has used FusionAuth for years. They say it does what Auth0 does but significantly cheaper, with self-hosting as an option.
"I've been forced (i.e., it was already decided) to use Auth0 before and I hated every minute of it."
Another developer was lukewarm: "Clerk seems fine, Auth0 is fine, but I'd rather build on open-source."
